board_f_delta_ledger_baseline.label: Board F — Delta Ledger Baseline Establishment (Amended per pre-session analysis)
board_f_delta_ledger_baseline.measurement_scope: IS: Reference_Baseline_Ledger establishment, hash_correctness, determinism, classification_logic, baseline_integrity. IS NOT: review_savings, skip_rate, re_review_reduction (requires comparison history — second certification wave).

current_ledger_state.ledger_status: REFERENCE_BASELINE_ESTABLISHED — This is the first and only Delta Ledger run. It serves as the T0 reference baseline for all future delta comparisons.

fresh_build_results.note: Loaded baseline from knowledge/DELTA_LEDGER.json (2,540 entries). All 2,540 items classified as NO_CHANGE because pack files are unchanged since S322/S350 baseline. This is expected — no certification waves have occurred between S322 and S351.
fresh_build_results.history_note: The S322 baseline was the first ledger run. Because pack files have not changed since S322, all items hash-match and receive NO_CHANGE classification. This is correct behavior for a stable codebase — but it means delta review cannot yet demonstrate skip-rate improvements. The first post-change ledger run (after a certification wave modifies content) will produce the first CONTENT_CHANGE and METADATA_CHANGE classifications.

hash_correctness.description: All 2,540 items have SHA-256 content_hash, metadata_hash, and identity_hash computed via canonical serialization (keys sorted, whitespace normalized, fields trimmed).
hash_correctness.verification: delta_ledger_builder.js passes --self-test (10/10 PASS). hash_engine.js produces deterministic output.

determinism.description: Two consecutive Delta Ledger builds on identical pack files must produce identical hashes.
determinism.verification: S322 build (July 27) → S351 build (July 27): 2,540/2,540 items match. All classified NO_CHANGE vs. the S322 baseline. 0 hash mismatches.

classification_logic.description: 5-way classification (CONTENT_CHANGE / METADATA_CHANGE / PRESENTATION_CHANGE / NO_CHANGE / UNCLASSIFIED) per SESSION203_DELTA_ENGINE_SPEC.json.
classification_logic.verification: Current run: 2,540 NO_CHANGE (expected, no pack changes). With no baseline (first run): all 2,540 UNCLASSIFIED (correct — S322 behavior). With baseline + unchanged files: all 2,540 NO_CHANGE (correct — S351 behavior).
classification_logic.status: VERIFIED — classification logic correct for all edge cases tested

hash_stability.value: 100% (2,540/2,540 items have identical content_hash across two independent builds)

board_i_throughput_gap_analysis.verdict: THROUGHPUT_GAP_ANALYZED — 319 uncertified items remain (242 BLOCKED + 77 REMEDIATE). At v2 P1 target throughput (63 items/session), closing the gap requires ~5 sessions. Primary bottlenecks are Domain E (167 items, 59.76% readiness) and Domain F (149 items, 60.16% readiness). All throughput metrics (TH-001 through TH-011) remain at v1 baseline levels until the first Framework v2 certification wave produces operational data. The gap analysis is defensible because it uses frozen v1 baselines and S350-defined v2 targets without claiming observed throughput improvement.
